newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares end down on technical correction.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares end down on technical correction.

text.p: Greek equities recovered slightly from their lowest ahead of the close, finishing 0.85 percent down on what analysts described as a technical correction.

They said future prospects were positive and they were watching for signals from a major government policy speech by Prime Minister Costas Simitis on Thursday and the 1997 budget due in late November.
"The market is in search of direction and today's drop does not impress me. It is purely technical," said Emmanuel Varsos, managing director at Investment Analysis SA told Reuters.
Varsos said the market wanted to hear specific measures to help the bourse from the government elected to a four-year term this month.
"The policy speech by Simitis is important but the 1997 budget is even more important because it spells out specific measures to attain budget deficit targets," he said.
Simitis will address parliament on his government's economic, domestic and foreign policy plans on October 10.
Varsos added that mid-term prospects for banks, food firms and cement companies were good but EPS growth projections for metallurgical firms were negative.
Investment Analysis in its mid-term bourse report which is revised on a weekly basis was bullish about the state National Bank of Greece, Heracles Cement and Inform Lykos.
He added that Alcatel and Aluminium of Greece were highly cyclical stocks, negatively correlated and Alcatel had the upper hand at this point in time.
The Athens general share index closed 0.85 percent, or 8.18 points lower at 955.29 from Monday's 963.47 close after opening at 963.47 points.
Turnover was slightly higher at 6.96 billion drachmas on volume of 4.19 million shares boosted by a block trade in Ergobank.

Gainers outpaced decliners 48 to 153 with 29 issues unchanged on 230 traded. Banks lost 1.02 percent, industrials fell 0.78 percent and construction retreated 1.02 percent. Small-caps fell 1.63 percent.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 543-561 at the close. Shares of OTE telecom OTEr.AT, the underlying, ended down 15 drachmas at 4,050.

The recently launched Merrill Lynch stock index call warrant based on a basket of 23 shares was higher at 193.60-203.80 drachmas. It expires on January 9 1998 with a strike price of 1000. It was in the money at 1044.6.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted lower at 4,563-4,870 drachmas at the close. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
